parsed.why: No trans criminalisation; services and hate-crime law cover gender identity, but enforcement is slow, officials hostile, and a majority disapproves of public LGBT expression. Conservative society with thin but real recourse: reduced risk.

Strong formal protections (self-ID floor, marriage, transfemicide law) undermined by documented police extortion of trans people, mass transfemicides and impunity warnings; rights rarely enjoyed in practice. No visitor facility/border rule: elevated risk.

Self-determination recognition, X marker, protected bathrooms, GI hate-crime coverage, working complaints body, dedicated LGBT+ travel guidance, broad social acceptance. No trans-specific exposure documented; only small hate-crime counts and unspecified gaps.

Active sodomy statute, a police Act clause used specifically against trans people, documented stripping and post-coup torture in detention, killings with no legal protections or confidence in courts; international advice to avoid entirely.

No recognition or protections, a latent entry ban on homosexual visitors, documented pattern of dating-app ambush attacks with most incidents unreported, and custody with no safe facilities. Recourse thin but no state campaign: elevated risk.
